title: 3. Schema & Distribution
description: Structural changes and statistical drift, with the uncertainty of each finding made explicit.

panels.title: Schema changes by classification
panels.description: ADDITIVE is routine. COLUMN_RENAME_CANDIDATE is a hypothesis, never a confirmed fact - a rename and a drop-plus-add are indistinguishable from the outside.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT change_type AS "change", count(*) AS "count"
                    FROM schema_changes GROUP BY change_type ORDER BY count(*) DESC

panels.title: Current schema fingerprint
panels.description: sha256 over the ordered (name, type, nullable) triples. A change here is a change in the contract surface, including a reordering.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT d.dataset_name AS "dataset",
                           left(s.fingerprint, 16) AS "fingerprint",
                           s.column_count AS "columns", s.captured_at AS "captured"
                    FROM (
                      SELECT DISTINCT ON (dataset_id) *
                      FROM schema_snapshots ORDER BY dataset_id, captured_at DESC
                    ) s JOIN datasets d USING (dataset_id)
                    ORDER BY d.dataset_name

panels.title: Detected schema changes
panels.description: `confidence` and `is_confirmed` only apply to rename candidates. The detector never sets is_confirmed - only a human or an explicit contract change can.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT sc.detected_at AS "when", d.dataset_name AS "dataset",
                           sc.change_type AS "change", sc.column_name AS "column",
                           COALESCE(sc.previous_column, '-') AS "was",
                           COALESCE(sc.previous_type, '-') AS "from_type",
                           COALESCE(sc.new_type, '-') AS "to_type",
                           sc.confidence AS "confidence",
                           sc.is_confirmed AS "confirmed",
                           sc.severity AS "severity"
                    FROM schema_changes sc JOIN datasets d USING (dataset_id)
                    WHERE $__timeFilter(sc.detected_at)
                    ORDER BY sc.detected_at DESC
                    LIMIT 100

panels.title: Drift statistic per column
panels.description: PSI for numeric columns, chi-square for categorical. An inconclusive test publishes NO statistic, so a gap here means the sample was below the contract minimum.

panels.title: Columns the drift test could not conclude on
panels.description: 1 means the sample was too small on at least one side, so no drift is claimed. This is a first-class outcome, not an error.

panels.title: Latest drift results
panels.description: `significant` is true only when the sample sizes met the minimum AND the statistic crossed a threshold. A large PSI on a tiny sample is never reported significant.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT d.dataset_name AS "dataset", dd.column_name AS "column",
                           dd.method AS "method", dd.statistic AS "statistic",
                           dd.p_value AS "p_value",
                           dd.reference_sample_size AS "n_ref",
                           dd.current_sample_size AS "n_cur",
                           dd.min_sample_size AS "n_min",
                           dd.status AS "status", dd.is_significant AS "significant"
                    FROM (
                      SELECT DISTINCT ON (dataset_id, column_name) *
                      FROM distribution_drift
                      ORDER BY dataset_id, column_name, evaluated_at DESC
                    ) dd JOIN datasets d USING (dataset_id)
                    ORDER BY dd.is_significant DESC, dd.statistic DESC NULLS LAST
